children: After a soft FY26, in which revenue growth decelerated to 5.8 per cent y-o-y (vs 3Y CAGR of 27 per cent) and EBITDA margin contracted about 651 bps to 51.2 per cent, we believe Central Depository Services (CDSL) is at the cusp of a volume-led growth recovery.

The two key headwinds are now behind. The pricing cuts in transaction charges and KYC (create and fetch), which dented KYC blended realisations by about 8-10 per cent, are fully in the base, and the heavy phase of technology and regulatory-led spending has largely played out. Primary market activity has turned decisively, with 50 mainboard IPOs in Q2-FY27 vs nine in Q1-FY27, and BO account additions have recovered to 1 lakh/day from a trough of 70K/day in March 2026.

We expect about 1 crore new accounts in Q2-FY27E (58 lakh in Q1FY27), the best quarterly addition in eight quarters. This should revive transaction revenue (almost flat for five quarters), KYC revenue and IPO/corporate action income (+18 per cent y-o-y in FY27E vs -1.9 per cent in FY26), while a widening issuer base compounds the annual issuer charge annuity (around 40 per cent of revenue).

The stock has underperformed over the past one year and is presently trading at a 42x FY28E which is about 7 per cent discount to its historical five-year average one-year forward P/E multiple of 45x.

This, in our view, prices in the FY26 slowdown but not the recovery. We upgrade CDSL to Buy from Add with a target price of ₹1,620, based on 45x Sep-28E EPS, in line with the 45-55x band the stock has commanded in previous growth-recovery phases.

title: Broker’s call: CDSL (Buy)
